title: NDPS special courts - how trial timelines actually work
p1:
Many people assume NDPS cases move quickly because they are handled by special courts.

The reality is more complex — a “special court” does not always mean a “fast trial.”
p2:
A common misconception is that NDPS special courts follow a completely different timeline from ordinary criminal courts.

In practice, they are designed for focused handling of drug-related offences, but the trial still depends on factors like investigation quality, evidence, witness availability, and court workload.
p3:
One lesser-known point: strict procedures around sampling, seizure records, forensic reports, and custody documentation can significantly affect how long a case takes.

A strong investigation can reduce delays, while missing links in evidence can slow proceedings for years.

The key takeaway: special courts provide a dedicated forum, not an automatic shortcut. Trial speed depends on how efficiently every stage — from investigation to evidence to hearings — is completed.
